notes: Tooling + docs only; zero platform-repo edits held across 288 iterations. The milestone existed because the platform is migrating its microservices back into `app` and nobody on our side knew how far that had got — the THIRD occurrence of one class (skiller v2.1, skillpath v2.7, jobsimulation now), each time re-derived from scratch. What breaks the cycle is not the re-point but the FENCE (clause 4) plus the written procedure (corpus/ops/platform-alignment.md, authored by iter-01 because it did not exist). Headline corrections that came from reading CODE and refuted a standing corpus claim: roadrunner was DELETED and replaced in-process, not merged into app (0 commits ever adding app/internal/roadrunner in a 6,728-ref clone); and cms's ECS service is DESTROYED, settled by cloning `infrastructure` — a repo that had never been in any clone set, which made the question look unmeasurable when it was only unclone d. TWO safety-relevant facts must survive this close: (1) a demo reached a PRODUCTION S3 bucket and only an IAM policy on an account we do not control refused it — iter-284's containment is proven by a unit test on the EMITTER and on NO RUNNING STACK, demo-2 predates it by nine hours, and the dev-side strip is demo-only; (2) the two tooling fixes landed at this close are in the rext AUTHORING copy and are NOT on a pushed tag, so no stack can obtain them until someone tags and pushes — tagging is not publishing.
